descriptionChirho: Core adjectival sense of being great, large, or significant in size, extent, importance, or intensity -- the primary meaning of the adjective covering physical magnitude, greatness of status, and general amplification. Arabic عَظِيم (ʿaẓīm) / كَبِير (kabīr) for greatness/largeness, Korean 큰 (keun) = big/great, Swahili kubwa/mkubwa = great/large. Includes all inflectional forms (ms, fs, mp, fp), article-prefixed forms, construct chains expressing quality (great-of), prepositional phrases (from-great, as-the-great, in/at-the-great), comparative uses (greater/greatest), and conjunctive forms (and-the-great).

Comparative sense denoting the elder or older of siblings or persons, used in birth-order and seniority contexts (e.g., 'the older daughter,' 'the firstborn'). Distinguished by Arabic الكُبرَى (al-kubrā, feminine superlative of kabīr) and الأكبَر (al-akbar, comparative) rather than عَظِيم; Spanish 'mayor' (elder) rather than 'grande'; Korean 큰 (keun) in familial contexts; Swahili mkubwa. BDB/HALOT sense: 'old, elder.'

Substantivized feminine plural (גְּדֹלוֹת) meaning 'great things,' 'great deeds,' or 'wonders' -- used absolutely or with prepositions to denote remarkable acts or events. Arabic عَظائِم (ʿaẓāʾim = great things/enormities), Korean 큰 일들을 (keun ildeul-eul = great things), Swahili mambo makubwa/mambo makuu (great matters). Includes both articled (the great things) and unarticled forms, and prepositional uses (in great things).

Sense denoting loudness or high volume when modifying voice (קוֹל) or sound, i.e., 'a great voice' = 'a loud voice.' Distinguished by Arabic عالٍ (ʿālin = high/loud) instead of عَظِيم, Hindi ऊँची (ūṁcī = high/loud), English 'loud / sound,' Spanish 'alta' (high). Korean 큰 (keun) remains, but the collocational domain is acoustic intensity. Swahili kubwa in this context means loud/great of volume.

Substantivized masculine plural/construct (גְּדוֹלִים, גְּדוֹלֵי) meaning 'great ones,' 'nobles,' or 'leaders' -- persons of high rank or authority. Arabic عُظَماء (ʿuẓamāʾ = nobles/magnates) and كِبار (kibār = great ones), Korean 큰 자들 (keun jadeul = great ones) and 높은 자들 (nopeun jadeul = lofty ones), Swahili wakubwa/wakuu (chiefs/great ones). Includes possessive-suffixed forms (his great ones, their greatest) and construct phrases (great-ones-of).

Infinitive absolute or verbal-adjective use expressing the process of becoming great or growing in magnitude/status -- a dynamic, progressive sense rather than a static quality. Arabic وَتَعاظُمًا (wa-taʿāẓuman = and becoming great) and يَعظَمُ (yaʿẓumu = he becomes great), Korean 커지며 (keojimyeo = becoming big) and 위대하며 (widaehamyeo = being great), Swahili kukua (to grow) and kuwa mkubwa (to become great). Overlaps morphologically with the verb H1431 גדל but tagged here under the adjective lemma.
